fields.why: The 2023 versus 2024 coverage contrasts (e.g., RSV 6.7% to 17.9%) use NHSN data but appear only in the Discussion, and the Limitations say they 'limit direct comparison'. Surveillance/descriptive alone fits the stated purpose; before/after is defensible under 'two time points compared'.

The county SVI is an area attribute linked to facilities and used as a stratifier; the brief excludes denominators but does not say how to treat linked area indexes. A rule such as 'list linked area indexes (SVI, ADI) in data_source_named only' would decide it, and readers in mm7343a3 split the same way.

The data are a nationwide set of CMS-certified nursing homes, and the region and state values are strata of those data. A's 'mixed' follows the literal wording 'national and subnational results reported together', since the text names South Dakota and North Dakota.

Age appears in the limitation 'vaccination data reported to NHSN are not disaggregated by age', which the brief records as a descriptor. A's added 'population' role is weaker, because the population is nursing home residents rather than an age group. The level is unaffected.
The Poisson models only produce coverage estimates and CIs and have no covariates; the brief says unadjusted is 'true also when the model itself has no covariates'.

The Methods state that the representativeness of voluntary reporters was assessed against all NHSN facilities, which is a selection-bias check but not a re-analysis of the model. The brief should say whether such a descriptive representativeness comparison counts as a 'bias check'.

brief_issues: The brief needs rules for three cases: a linked area index (SVI) as a data_source_type, whether region or state strata of national data make a setting 'mixed', and whether a representativeness comparison of reporters counts as a sensitivity or bias check.
